newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai sets 80 trillion won sales goal for '97.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai sets 80 trillion won sales goal for '97.

text.p: The Hyundai Group, South Korea's largest conglomerate in terms of assets, said on Tuesday it had set an 80 trillion won target for this year's sales by its member firms, up from an estimated 70 trillion won in 1996.

A Hyundai statement said it targeted raising exports by its 50 member firms, that include carmaker Hyundai Motor Co and chipmaker Hyundai Electronics Industries Co, to $17.3 billion from $15.2 billion in 1996.
A breakdown by company was not immediately available.
The statement said Hyundai planned to increase investment in facilities and in research and development projects to nine trillion won from an estimated 8.2 trillion won in 1996.
The group also plans to transfer manufacturing operations in 12 categories, from which annual sales are valued at a combined 41.73 billion won, to non-member small and medium-sized firms.
The move is in line with the group's long-standing strategy of streamlining its business operations, the statement said.
Financial terms of such transfers were not given.
